title: FOMC minutes of the December 7-8, 2027 meeting (the year's final SEP) — D+21 lands in the dead week, and the Board's own holiday calendar says that is fine
source: EST: the Board's own publication rule applied to its own 2027 panel, with the displacement risk both seeding proposals flagged measured against the Board's OWN closure calendar rather than against the market's. THE RULE is verbatim from federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, re-fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes, stamp 'Last Update: August 19, 2026'): 'The minutes of regularly scheduled meetings are released three weeks after the date of the policy decision.' THE MEETING is that page's 2027 panel, 'December 7-8*', the asterisk being 'Meeting associated with a Summary of Economic Projections'; 2027-12-07 is a Tuesday and 2027-12-08 a Wednesday (computed, not assumed), so the decision is Wednesday 2027-12-08 and D+21 is Wednesday 2027-12-29. THE CENSUS IS THIS SESSION'S OWN PARSE, not inherited: fomccalendars.htm plus fomchistorical2007.htm through fomchistorical2020.htm (fifteen pages, HTTP 200 each), each meeting block's minutes link -- both the pre-2008 /fomc/minutes/YYYYMMDD form and the later fomcminutesYYYYMMDD form -- paired to that block's own '(Released ...)' string, blocks cut at the next panel boundary first. It returns 157 releases, decisions 2007-01-31 through 2026-07-29, exactly 8 per year 2007-2025, of which 143 sit at exactly D+21 with 14 exceptions running D+19 to D+24 -- reproducing the fomc-minutes-2027-11-17 and fomc-minutes-2027-10-06 lanes instance for instance from an independent construction. THE DECEMBER CLASS, AND THE CORRECTION THE PROPOSALS NEEDED: 19 December meetings, 4 displaced (21.1%), and displacement is fully explained by distance to the BOARD OF GOVERNORS' own year-end closure, not by the Christmas-New Year window. Board closures come from federalreserve.gov/aboutthefed/k8.htm ('Holidays Observed by the Federal Reserve System 2026-2030', HTTP 200, 82,205 bytes, stamp 'Last Update: July 8, 2026'). Bucketed by min|gap| from D+21 to the nearest Board closure: |gap|<=1 runs 4 displaced of 5, |gap|>=2 runs 0 displaced of 14, and four of those holds sit at exactly |gap|=2. 2027-12-29 SITS AT |gap|=2 -- five days after the Board's Christmas closure (Fri 2027-12-24) and two days before its New Year closure (Fri 2027-12-31, which k8.htm names outright in its footnote: 'the Federal Reserve Banks are open, but the Board of Governors is closed on ... December 24, 2027, December 31, 2027'). THE WINDOW HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED BY THE ONLY OBSERVATION THAT COULD TEST IT: the from-fomc-2027-12-08 proposal's worry was that a dead-week placement has no precedent, citing 2025-12-10 whose D+21 (Fri 2025-12-31) was pulled forward. It was pulled forward to TUESDAY 2025-12-30 -- inside the dead week. A Board avoiding the week would have gone to January; it moved one day and stayed. AND THE TWIN IS ALREADY ON THE BOOKS: fomc-minutes-2026-12-30 (confirmed, FED: the Board's own December 2026 month page listing 'FOMC Minutes' at 2:00 p.m.) is the identical geometry -- Wednesday, dead week, gap +5 from the Christmas closure and -2 from the New Year closure, third of four open Board days in a bracketed week. Filed estimate on the same limit the sibling records: a firm publication convention cannot outrank a tentative input, and the same page states 'Each meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it', so the promotion trigger is the 2027-10-26/27 meeting ratifying December 7-8, not a better fetch. The 14:00 ET release time is the Board's standing convention and is not stated on this page. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by the fomc-minutes-2027-12-29 initial-research lane (2026-09-08) after reading BOTH prior proposals -- from-fomc-2027-12-08 and from-fomc-blackout-start-2027-11-27 -- which are now inert and stay where they are. Every claim was re-derived from primaries. BOTH PROPOSALS' CONCLUSIONS HOLD; THEIR SHARED WORRY IS RETIRED. from-fomc-2027-12-08 filed the date 'with an unusually loud caveat', reading the December record as '4 of 5 December meetings released at exactly D+21 ... and ALL FOUR LANDED IN JANUARY', with the lone exception the one whose D+21 fell in the Christmas-New Year window. That census was the live page alone (2021-2026). The full 21-year census is 19 December meetings with FOUR displacements, and once measured against the Board's own K.8 closure calendar the pattern is not about the window at all: |gap|<=1 to a Board closure runs 4 of 5 displaced, |gap|>=2 runs 0 of 14, and 2027 sits at |gap|=2 with four in-bucket holds (2016, 2017, 2022, 2023). THE GENERALISABLE RESULT is a method result and it is the December analogue of the sibling's Thanksgiving finding: the Thanksgiving gap is QUANTISED (a fixed Thursday against a weekday-preserving D+21, so offsets are multiples of 7 +/-1), while the year-end gap is CONTINUOUS (New Year's Day is a fixed calendar date whose weekday drifts), so a December lane cannot borrow the sibling's clean bucket structure and must compute the gap in days. THE HONEST LIMIT, STATED NOT SMOOTHED: all four |gap|=2 holds are on the +2 side; 2027 is the first -2 case in the meeting record. It is not untested for long -- fomc-minutes-2026-12-30 is the exact structural twin (same weekday, same dead week, same +5/-2 gaps, same third-of-four-open-days position) and it is CONFIRMED on the Board's own December 2026 month page, so the Board has already scheduled a release at this geometry; and 2025's remedy for a gap -1 D+21 was to move TO gap -2. WHAT THE TAPE WORK ADDS, and it is a refusal that no sibling could have made: the December class's release-day statistics DO NOT TRANSFER TO THIS DATE, because 18 of the 19 historical December-class releases landed in the January 1-8 window and 2027-12-29 would land in the December 26-31 window, and those two windows are opposite regimes. Over 4,949 sessions 2007-01-04 to 2026-09-04 (CBOE SPX/VIX fetched today; anchors SPX 7,718.60 / VIX 14.53 at 2026-09-04): Jan 1-8 runs VIX-down 66.3% (n=95), Dec 26-31 runs VIX-down 37.2% (n=78) against a 54.4% universe -- a 29.1pp swing at permutation P < 0.00001. And the release adds NOTHING over its window: the 18 January releases run 72.2% VIX-down against their own window's 66.3%, P = 0.633, with every other measure at P >= 0.63. So the family's headline vol number is a calendar-window artifact on this class, and 2027 moves the release into the window that points the other way. The December class itself is a clean null against the universe on every measure (mean|S&P| 0.703% P = 0.653, up-share 52.6% P = 1.000, VIX-down 68.4% P = 0.256, residualised dVIX -0.054 P = 0.814) -- the family's index null replicates a fifth time. THREE DATED ADJACENCIES PROPOSED IN THE SAME PR, each load-bearing: vix-expiration-2027-12-15 (D-14, from the OCC's own 2027 calendar; December was the gap in this calendar's vix-expiration series and the sibling's settlement-collision split cannot be evaluated without it -- this release is OFF-settlement), fed-board-closure-2027-12-31 (D+2, the exact closure this entry's date rule is measured against, and the one 2027 date where the Board is shut while the NYSE and OCC are open and running a quarterly expiration) and fomc-2028-01-26 (D+28, the Board's own 2027-panel footnote 'A two-day meeting is scheduled for January 25-26, 2028'; this calendar carries ZERO 2028 entries). SAME CHANNEL CAVEAT AS EVERY MACRO ENTRY: symbols is empty and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates- or minutes-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; nothing here licenses an entry.
